title: Who Is Jesus?
subtitle: The Messiah's worship, the strongest Christian objection, and Islam's invitation to follow him
summary: Islam honors Jesus as the Messiah and a mighty messenger, while giving worship to the God he served. His prayers, need for God, and references to his own God support that view. Christian texts about his divinity need a real answer, not dismissal. Islam joins this reading of Jesus's life with reasons to trust the Quran.

seo.metaTitle: Who Is Jesus? The Islamic and Christian Answers Compared
seo.metaDescription: Jesus's worship, the strongest Christian divinity texts, and Islam's reasoned invitation to honor the Messiah while worshiping his God.

sections.title: Honor the Messiah, Worship His God
sections.body:
Islam does not ask people to dismiss Jesus. It affirms his virgin birth (Quran 3:47), miracles, and title of Messiah. It also identifies him as God's servant and messenger. Its call is to follow his devotion to the Creator rather than worship him.

There are reasons behind that call: Jesus prays, receives authority, and speaks of his God. These fit the work of a prophet. Christianity offers another explanation that deserves a fair hearing. The [case for trusting the Quran](/articles/why-the-quran) also matters. Muslims believe God revealed it to correct later disputes about Jesus.

sections.title: Why the Question Matters
sections.body:
Love for Jesus is not what separates the two faiths. They disagree about the kind of honor he should receive. If he is divine, worshiping him follows Christian belief. If he is God's human messenger, the same act gives a servant what belongs to the Creator.

This deserves more than counting verses or defending a religious label. It concerns whom to pray to and who gives life. Islam offers a way to keep love for the Messiah and worship of God alone together.

sections.title: What Would Establish His Identity?
sections.body:
A miraculous birth or an extraordinary deed does not, by itself, prove that someone is God. Christians and Muslims both regard Adam as human despite his unusual origin. A miracle worked through someone can likewise show God's support without proving that person is the source of its power.

The key questions concern Jesus's relationship to God, his teaching about worship, and the trustworthiness of the records about him. Islam brings those questions together. Its argument is not simply that one exact English sentence is missing from the Gospels.

sections.title: Read the Gospels Before Debating Church Councils
sections.body:
The Gospels place Jesus in a Jewish setting shaped by worship of the one God. They also use the high titles and descriptions on which Christians base their belief about him. An honest comparison must read both.

Later councils defined the Trinity and incarnation. That does not prove the beliefs began at those councils. Christians see the definitions as faithful accounts of earlier testimony. What matters is whether that reading best explains the evidence, not just whether its terms came later.

sections.title: The Quran's Portrait of Jesus
sections.body:
In Quran 19:30-31, Jesus calls himself God's servant. God gives him revelation and makes him a prophet. He is commanded to pray and give charity. Quran 3:45 honors him as Messiah; Quran 5:110 says his miracles occur by God's permission. His honor and his need for God appear together.

Quran 4:171 calls him God's messenger and word, while warning against excess in beliefs about him. Quran 3:59 links his creation with God's command and the example of Adam. In the Quran's account, his title does not make him a second divine person.

In Quran 5:72, Jesus tells people to worship Allah. Allah is his Lord and their Lord. These passages explain what Islam teaches about Jesus. To accept them as true, a non-Muslim also needs reasons to trust the Quran as revelation; citing the verses alone cannot supply those reasons.

sections.title: The Strong Christian Objection
sections.body:
John 1:1, Thomas's words to Jesus in John 20:28, Colossians 1:15-17, and Hebrews 1:3 are important evidence for Christian belief. Thomas speaks directly to Jesus. His words cannot simply be dismissed as a cry aimed elsewhere.

Christianity explains Jesus's prayer through the incarnation: God the Son lives a truly human life. The [official Catholic account, sections 464-475](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_one/section_two/chapter_two/artcile_3.html) holds his humanity and divinity together. Prayer alone does not logically disprove that belief.

Muslims give greater weight to another relationship. In John 17:3, Jesus calls the Father the only true God; in John 20:17, he speaks of his own God. These concern who receives worship and has authority over Jesus, not just his physical hunger. Islam reads this as a prophet's relationship with God. Christians read it through the Son's humanity while still calling him divine. [The Divinity Verses Examined](/articles/the-divinity-verses-examined) weighs that reading passage by passage.

sections.title: Why His Relationship to God Still Matters
sections.body:
Mark 12:29 records Jesus affirming the one God. In John 17:3 he calls the Father the only true God and distinguishes himself as the one sent. John 20:17 has him speak of his God and his followers' God. John 5:30 describes his need for God rather than action from himself alone. Acts 2:22 describes God working through him.

These statements form a pattern. God sends Jesus and gives him power. Jesus receives his mission and power from God, and Jesus worships God. Muslims find that a prophet's role explains the pattern directly. Worship belongs to the One who grants authority, rather than the one who receives it.

Christians read the same passages through the Son's human nature. The dispute is not that either side has overlooked prayer. It is whether the whole record warrants calling the worshiper himself divine.

sections.title: Why Islam Chooses the Prophetic Reading
sections.body:
Islam connects Jesus's words about God with the way he lives. He is sent, not self-appointed. He receives authority rather than being its ultimate source, and he speaks of having a God. Worship follows that relationship: it is given to the One he serves. This is the positive force of reading Jesus as a prophet, not just noting that he ate or prayed.

John's high language remains real evidence for Christians. Islam does not claim that every New Testament sentence already teaches what the Quran teaches. It claims that God sent a correction, with reasons of its own to be trusted. Two examples help explain those reasons.

The transmitted [eclipse report in Sahih al-Bukhari 1043](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1043) describes Muhammad rejecting a flattering claim about his family. That weighs against a simple account of a man seeking personal gain, though not every account of sincere human error. Physical witnesses such as the [Birmingham Quran leaves](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/news-archive/2015/birmingham-quran-manuscript-dated-among-the-oldest-in-the-world) give access to early transmission. Radiocarbon dates their parchment, not the act of writing. Neither fact proves revelation alone. Alongside a message that refuses to make its messenger divine, they link the teaching, the man's conduct, and early access to the text.

[Why the Quran?](/articles/why-the-quran) and [Who Is Prophet Muhammad?](/articles/who-is-prophet-muhammad) develop these links and examine other explanations. This is why Muslims can see the Quran's account of Jesus as a correction supported by reasons, rather than a later opinion that demands assent.

sections.title: Miracles, Titles, and Respect
sections.body:
The virgin birth does not force a choice between denying a miracle and worshiping its recipient. Islam accepts the miracle and credits it to the Creator. Quran 3:59 gives Adam as the comparison.

Refusing to worship Jesus is not, in Islam, refusing to honor him. Being a messenger gives people a reason to heed his call, not to replace the God he served. Quran 5:75 calls Jesus a messenger and his mother truthful, while noting their human need for food.

Nor do Christians intend to worship three independent gods. Their belief needs to be answered as they teach it. Honest disagreement builds more trust than an easy but false description.

sections.title: Following Jesus Without Dividing Worship
sections.body:
Islam offers a life that follows Jesus's devotion: prayer to God, humility, charity, repentance, and trust in the Creator. Jesus remains loved as Messiah and messenger. Worship remains with the source of his mission.

Two questions belong together: how best to understand Jesus's relationship to God, and whether the Quran has good grounds to clarify it. Someone convinced by those reasons has grounds to embrace Islam, not merely admire a comparison of beliefs. [What Is Salvation?](/articles/what-is-salvation) explains the hope and duties that follow.

sections.title: The Question to Carry Forward
sections.body: Islam joins Jesus's honor with his service to God and gives worship to his God alone. His prayer and need for God support that reading, but the Christian reply deserves study. [Did Jesus Worship God?](/articles/did-jesus-worship-god) explores his devotion, while [how divine revelation can be recognized](/articles/what-is-revelation) takes up the question of revelation.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.body:
Q: Does Islam require belief in Jesus?
A: Yes. Islam honors him as the Messiah and God's messenger. Quran 3:45 and 19:30 join his great honor with his role as a human prophet.

Q: Does Jesus praying automatically disprove Christian belief?
A: No. Christians explain his prayer through the incarnation and a real human nature. Muslims find that his worship, need for God, and mission are better explained by prophethood. This takes reasoning, not a one-line gotcha.

Q: Does Islam have to deny John 20:28 to make its case?
A: No. Thomas addresses Jesus in that passage. An honest Islamic reading takes this seriously alongside Jesus's words about his own God. It must also explain why the Quran is trusted as a correction.

Q: Does following Jesus mean knowing the answer to every theological dispute first?
A: Study of his devotion to God and prayer for guidance can begin before every dispute is settled. Accepting Islam calls for conviction about God's oneness and Muhammad's message, not mastery of every debate.

sections.title: Further Reading
sections.body: Selected sources and further reading are listed below.

quranVerses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ ٱللَّهُ يَٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ ٱذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِى عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَتِكَ إِذْ أَيَّدتُّكَ بِرُوحِ ٱلْقُدُسِ تُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًۭا ۖ وَإِذْ عَلَّمْتُكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَٱلتَّوْرَىٰةَ وَٱلْإِنجِيلَ ۖ وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ مِنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ بِإِذْنِى فَتَنفُخُ فِيهَا فَتَكُونُ طَيْرًۢا بِإِذْنِى ۖ وَتُبْرِئُ ٱلْأَكْمَهَ وَٱلْأَبْرَصَ بِإِذْنِى ۖ وَإِذْ تُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِى ۖ وَإِذْ كَفَفْتُ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ عَنكَ إِذْ جِئْتَهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ فَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
quranVerses.translation: [The Day] when Allah will say, "O Jesus, Son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Pure Spirit and you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity; and [remember] when I taught you writing and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you designed from clay [what was] like the form of a bird with My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird with My permission; and you healed the blind and the leper with My permission; and when you brought forth the dead with My permission; and when I restrained the Children of Israel from [killing] you when you came to them with clear proofs and those who disbelieved among them said, "This is not but obvious magic."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍۢ مِّنْهُ ٱسْمُهُ ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَجِيهًۭا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
quranVerses.translation: [And mention] when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary - distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near [to Allah].
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَيُكَلِّمُ ٱلنَّاسَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًۭا وَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
quranVerses.translation: He will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity and will be of the righteous."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَتْ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى وَلَدٌۭ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌۭ ۖ قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ ۚ إِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمْرًۭا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
quranVerses.translation: She said, "My Lord, how will I have a child when no man has touched me?" [The angel] said, "Such is Allah; He creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَا تَغْلُوا۟ فِى دِينِكُمْ وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلْحَقَّ ۚ إِنَّمَا ٱلْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُۥٓ أَلْقَىٰهَآ إِلَىٰ مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌۭ مِّنْهُ ۖ فَـَٔامِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦ ۖ وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ ثَلَٰثَةٌ ۚ ٱنتَهُوا۟ خَيْرًۭا لَّكُمْ ۚ إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۖ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥٓ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌۭ ۘ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلًۭا
quranVerses.translation: O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion or say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a soul [created at a command] from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say, "Three"; desist - it is better for you. Indeed, Allah is but one God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: مَّا ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌۭ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُۥ صِدِّيقَةٌۭ ۖ كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ ٱلطَّعَامَ ۗ ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ ٱلْءَايَٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱنظُرْ أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ
quranVerses.translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَالَ إِنِّى عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ ءَاتَىٰنِىَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَجَعَلَنِى نَبِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: [Jesus] said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَجَعَلَنِى مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ وَأَوْصَٰنِى بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَتِى وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِى جَبَّارًۭا شَقِيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: And [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَٱلسَّلَٰمُ عَلَىَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّۭا
quranVerses.translation: And peace is on me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَقَفَّيْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ بِٱلرُّسُلِ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَا عِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَأَيَّدْنَٰهُ بِرُوحِ ٱلْقُدُسِ ۗ أَفَكُلَّمَا جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌۢ بِمَا لَا تَهْوَىٰٓ أَنفُسُكُمُ ٱسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ فَفَرِيقًۭا كَذَّبْتُمْ وَفَرِيقًۭا تَقْتُلُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And We did certainly give Moses the Torah and followed up after him with messengers. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Pure Spirit. But is it [not] that every time a messenger came to you, [O Children of Israel], with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? And a party [of messengers] you denied and another party you killed.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: وَرَسُولًا إِلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ ۖ أَنِّىٓ أَخْلُقُ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطِّينِ كَهَيْـَٔةِ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَأَنفُخُ فِيهِ فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًۢا بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَأُبْرِئُ ٱلْأَكْمَهَ وَٱلْأَبْرَصَ وَأُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ فِى بُيُوتِكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
quranVerses.translation: And [make him] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [who will say], 'Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord in that I design for you from clay [that which is] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah. And I cure the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead - by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: لَقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ۖ وَقَالَ ٱلْمَسِيحُ يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبَّكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُۥ مَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَمَأْوَىٰهُ ٱلنَّارُ ۖ وَمَا لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ مِنْ أَنصَارٍۢ
quranVerses.translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary" while the Messiah has said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ ءَادَمَ ۖ خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
quranVerses.translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created Him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
Jesus answered, “The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one:
Jesus said to her, “Don’t hold me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers, and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’”

Behold, one came to him and said, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?” He said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”
I can of myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge, and my judgment is righteous; because I don’t seek my own will, but the will of my Father who sent me.
“Men of Israel, hear these words! Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which God did by him among you, even as you yourselves know,
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

faq.question: Does Islam require belief in Jesus?
faq.answer: Yes. Islam honors him as the Messiah and God's messenger. Quran 3:45 and 19:30 join his great honor with his role as a human prophet.

faq.question: Does Jesus praying automatically disprove Christian belief?
faq.answer: No. Christians explain his prayer through the incarnation and a real human nature. Muslims find that his worship, need for God, and mission are better explained by prophethood. This takes reasoning, not a one-line gotcha.

faq.question: Does Islam have to deny John 20:28 to make its case?
faq.answer: No. Thomas addresses Jesus in that passage. An honest Islamic reading takes this seriously alongside Jesus's words about his own God. It must also explain why the Quran is trusted as a correction.

faq.question: Does following Jesus mean knowing the answer to every theological dispute first?
faq.answer: Study of his devotion to God and prayer for guidance can begin before every dispute is settled. Accepting Islam calls for conviction about God's oneness and Muhammad's message, not mastery of every debate.
